questions.question: How should drivers who talk to passengers be viewed?
questions.explanation: Talking with passengers takes a driver's attention away from the road. Be careful when driving near distracted drivers.

questions.question: Which sign means brakes need repair?

options.text: Brake pads are not covered in grease.
Brake pads are not covered in oil.

questions.explanation: Check your brakes for cracked drums, shoes or pads covered in oil or grease, and shoes that are worn dangerously thin, broken, or missing.

questions.question: When should you adjust mirrors?
questions.explanation: Always check and adjust mirrors before you start driving. If your vehicle has a trailer, make sure it is straight so you can check the mirrors correctly.

questions.question: Why is rolling backward when you start to accelerate dangerous?

options.text: The truck is not made to go backwards.
You may hit a vehicle behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may hit a vehicle behind you.
questions.explanation: Make sure you can accelerate without rolling backward. Rolling backward can cause you to hit a vehicle or obstacle behind your truck.

questions.question: When driving a 50-foot truck at 50 mph, what is the minimum following distance?
questions.explanation: Below 40 mph, allow one second of following distance for every 10 feet of vehicle length. At higher speeds, use the same formula and add one more second.

questions.question: When backing a trailer, what should you do first?

options.text: Turn the steering wheel in the direction of the turn.
Turn the steering wheel in the direction opposite of the turn.
Turn the wheel as sharply as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the steering wheel in the direction opposite of the turn.
questions.explanation: With a straight truck, turn the wheel toward where you want to go. With a trailer, turn the wheel the opposite way first. Once the trailer starts to turn, turn the wheel the other way to follow it.

questions.question: On a curve, the posted speed limit:

options.text: Can still cause a vehicle to tip over.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can still cause a vehicle to tip over.
questions.explanation: The posted speed on a curve may be safe for cars but too fast for larger vehicles like trucks. Driving a truck at the posted limit on a curve can cause it to tip over.

questions.question: If a vehicle has an inspection report, what should a driver do?

options.text: Inspect the vehicle first, then compare notes with the report.
Read the report first when inspecting the vehicle.
Skip the inspection and only use the report.

questions.correctAnswerText: Read the report first when inspecting the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Start your vehicle inspection by reviewing the report left by the previous driver.

questions.question: What removes alcohol from your bloodstream?
questions.explanation: Your body removes alcohol at a fixed rate. Coffee and exercise cannot speed this up. Only time allows your body to remove alcohol.

questions.question: During a static leakage test, what is the maximum safe leak rate for a double combination vehicle?
questions.explanation: A double combination vehicle with air brakes should leak no more than 3 psi in one minute. If it leaks faster, something needs repair and the vehicle should not be driven.

questions.question: During an inspection, the release arm should be properly seated and the safety latch or lock should be:
questions.explanation: Before a trip, check the fifth wheel. Make sure the release arm is seated correctly and the safety latch or lock is engaged. All parts should be present and working properly.

questions.question: What should you do when confronted with an aggressive driver?

options.text: Try to stay in the other driver's way.

questions.explanation: If you meet an aggressive driver, get out of their way. Do not make eye contact. Do not speed up to challenge them. Do not react to angry gestures.

questions.question: If a truck has one, a trailer brake hand valve can be used to:

options.text: Prevent the truck from rolling back when starting from a stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prevent the truck from rolling back when starting from a stop.
questions.explanation: A trailer brake hand valve can stop the vehicle from rolling backward when you start from a stop.

questions.question: A broken exhaust system can:

options.text: Allow poisonous fumes to enter the cab.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow poisonous fumes to enter the cab.
questions.explanation: A broken exhaust system is dangerous. It can allow poisonous fumes to enter the cab or sleeper berth.

questions.question: When coupling a double or triple, which trailer should you attach last?

options.text: The trailer directly behind the cab

questions.explanation: When coupling double or triple trailers, attach the back trailer last.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a vehicle inspection report?

options.text: It tells the motor carrier about problems that need fixing.
It ensures the vehicle is inspected regularly.
It holds drivers responsible for inspecting their vehicles.
It provides a plan for the next five trips.

questions.correctAnswerText: It tells the motor carrier about problems that need fixing.
questions.explanation: A vehicle inspection report tells the motor carrier about issues that could affect safe operation. Complete one after each day of driving. Note any problems that could affect safety or cause a mechanical breakdown.

questions.question: When backing, you should:

options.text: Move quickly to get out of the way of other drivers.
Try not to use your mirrors.

questions.explanation: Backing a large truck is dangerous because you cannot see everything behind you. If you must back up, use a helper if you can.

questions.question: What is a wig wag?

options.text: A tube that moves air from the compressor to the tanks
A noise made by air brakes when used
A part in the braking unit that allows air to move freely

questions.explanation: A wig wag is a low air pressure warning device in an air brake system. It drops a mechanical arm into your view when air pressure drops below 60 psi.

questions.question: What is the average driver's reaction time?
questions.explanation: The average driver reacts in three-quarters of a second to one second. At 55 mph, you travel about 61 feet during this time.

questions.question: When transporting cargo, you must check that it is secure every:
questions.explanation: Check cargo securement before you start, within the first 50 miles, and then every three hours or 150 miles.
